title: Tourist spots 'dark, mound-like shape' in Loch Ness on family holiday in Scotland
excerpt: A tourist visiting Loch Ness has reported seeing a dark, mound-like shape appearing to rise from the water, sparking the latest potential sighting of the legendary Loch Ness Monster.
content:
A tourist visiting Loch Ness has reported seeing a "dark, mound-like shape" appearing to rise from the water, sparking the latest potential sighting of the legendary Loch Ness Monster.

Another Nessie sighting has been recorded

Jocelyn Boyce, who was visiting Scotland with her family from Barcelona, Spain, said she spotted the unusual shape while at Urquhart Castle in August.

The visitor was looking out over the famous loch when she noticed something moving in the water and quickly used her phone to capture photographs and video footage.

Boyce later submitted her report and images to the Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register, detailing the moment she saw what she described as a dark shape protruding above the surface.

She said: "I was at a viewpoint at Urquhart Castle overlooking Loch Ness with my family when we noticed a dark, almost black, mound-like shape protruding above the surface of the water.

"I initially observed the object with my naked eye. I estimate that it was approximately half a mile away from our position.

"The water appeared calm and general visibility was good."

Boyce said she recorded around 13 seconds of footage using an iPhone 16 and used the phone’s zoom function because of the distance between herself and the object.

She added: "I took approximately 13 seconds of video footage using an iPhone 16.

"Due to the distance, I used the phone’s zoom while recording the video. The dark mound-like shape is visible above the surface of the water in one of my photographs.

"In another photograph taken moments later, the object is no longer visible above the water."

The report is the latest in a series of claimed Nessie sightings, with reports appearing to have increased in 2026 compared with the previous year.

The rise in sightings comes after experts previously warned that a lack of reports could suggest the famous creature had disappeared.

According to the Daily Star newspaper, Rob Long, from the Loch Ness Exploration [LNE] team said: "There is a real fear for her as it normally is not this long that we go without a single glimpse.

"Normally people from our team will see her but so far, none of us have. Others have claimed to but we have not seen waters this quiet."

Long said that while sightings had become less frequent over the years, some previous reports had provided stronger evidence.

He added: "The viewings have gotten less over the years, but never this scarce for us. Despite the lack of viewings, 2024 was the year we got the most definitive proof that Nessie exists - with the sonar recordings among the best we have ever got."

The Loch Ness Monster remains one of Scotland’s most famous legends, with visitors continuing to search the waters in the hope of catching a glimpse of the mysterious creature.
